i18n.hindiRisk: SEVERE. The one screen in the app whose entire job is language choice contains zero stringResource calls — every string is a literal (lines 67, 69, 105, 110, 116). It hardcodes a Hindi subtitle (:69) next to English body copy (:105, :110, :116), so every user sees a mixed-language screen regardless of device locale, and a Hindi-first Ayodhya user is asked to 'Continue' in English. Layout-wise the sheet is a fixed 72% fillMaxHeight with no verticalScroll (:95, :100), so if these strings were ever translated (Devanagari runs 15-30% longer and taller) the Spacer(weight 1f) at :115 would collapse and the Continue button could be pushed off the fixed-height sheet on small screens. surfaces.density: Airy to the point of emptiness. The sheet is a fixed 72% of screen height (:95) holding only a heading, one line of sub-copy, two 16dp-padded radio rows, and a button, with a Spacer(weight 1f) at :115 absorbing the remainder — roughly the bottom third of the sheet is dead space on a typical phone. Padding values used: 28/24/24 sheet (:101), 16dp item spacing (:102), 16dp inside each option row (LanguagePickerCard.kt:61).

observations.claim: The language-selection screen — the literal first pixel of the product for an Ayodhya user — has zero localization: all five user-facing strings are Kotlin literals, and it mixes a hardcoded Hindi subtitle with hardcoded English body copy and CTA.

The most prominent text on the screen (the language names 'English' / 'हिन्दी') renders in the unmapped titleMedium slot, so it falls back to Roboto while the hero wordmark above it renders in Geist via headlineLarge — two typefaces visible simultaneously in the first frame of the app.
There is no loading, error, or disabled state on Continue; setAppLocale is awaited in a coroutine with no failure path, so a failed locale write silently strands the user on the screen.
The sheet radius (24dp, :96) is off the HomeservicesRadius scale (max xl=20) and the option cards inside it use a different radius (16dp), so three different corner radii stack within one screen.

The sheet uses colorScheme.background (#FBF7EF) while the immediately following AuthScreen sheet — identical geometry, identical 24dp radius, identical 8dp elevation — uses colorScheme.surface (#FFFDF8), so the sheet colour shifts between two consecutive onboarding screens.

No navigationBarsPadding on the sheet; the Continue button's 24dp bottom padding (:101) is the only clearance from the gesture bar, and HsPrimaryButton is a fixed 64dp tall (design-system HsComponents.kt:44).
Bottom third of the sheet is dead space — a Spacer(weight 1f) separates a 4-element form from the CTA inside a fixed 72%-height sheet, with no imagery, illustration, or value proposition to fill it.
Zero motion: language selection is an instant colour swap with no state transition, and no HomeservicesMotion token is referenced anywhere in the file.
Hero decorative circles use literal Color.White while the visually identical hero on AuthScreen uses colorScheme.onPrimary for the same circles — the two heroes will diverge in dark theme.

surfaces.density: Two incompatible densities in one screen. The AuthFrame states are airy — 24dp sheet padding, space6 (24dp) between blocks (:257), inside a card that itself adds space4 (design-system/.../HsComponents.kt:120) — while LoadingContent is a sparse, centre-of-void layout with 32dp padding and nothing else (:604). Within EmailEntry the vertical rhythm is inconsistent: 12dp between the fields (:422) but 20dp above the CTA (:446), then three stacked full-width TextButtons (:459, :466) with only default button padding between them.

observations.claim: Every error message the user can ever see on the auth screen is a hardcoded English string literal in the ViewModel, so a Hindi-locale user hits English error copy on the single most failure-prone screen in the app.
Six of eleven auth states replace the entire branded hero+sheet shell with a bare, unstyled centered CircularProgressIndicator — the app visually disappears every time the user taps a sign-in method.

Flat-card-on-flat-sheet: HsSectionCard is given containerColor = colorScheme.surface and 1dp elevation, and AuthFrame's sheet is also colorScheme.surface, so the content card is the exact same colour as the surface behind it and is separated only by a 1dp shadow.

The Google sign-in button uses a hand-rolled circle containing the letter 'G' in Roboto (labelMedium is unmapped) tinted #1A73E8, rather than the official Google mark — it reads as a placeholder and is the primary CTA of the screen.
Zero motion in a 662-line multi-state screen: eleven states hard-cut with no Crossfade or AnimatedContent, and no HomeservicesMotion/HomeservicesEasing token is imported.

The three sign-in methods are rendered as three identical HsActionButtons with identical weight and styling — there is no visually preferred/primary path, so the user must read all three before choosing.
Hindi labels on the three method buttons will be truncated rather than wrapped: HsActionButton pins height to 52.dp and the label to maxLines = 1 with ellipsis.
A decorative 40x2dp bar is drawn at the top of the sheet, mimicking a bottom-sheet drag handle on a sheet that cannot be dragged.
No TalkBack heading is exposed for the actual task title of any auth state — HsScreenTitle is only applied to the brand wordmark, while the per-state title at :269 is a plain Text.

In EmailEntry the first focusable control inside the card is the 'Back to sign-in options' TextButton, placed above the email field, so assistive-tech and keyboard users reach the escape hatch before the form.

No offline state exists in AuthUiState; connectivity failures degrade into the generic 'Sign-in failed. Please try again.' error, which is the wrong message for the target market's network conditions.

The Error state discards all user context — the typed email/phone and the chosen method are not carried into AuthUiState.Error, so 'Try again' returns the user to a re-entry flow rather than to their filled form.
OTP entry is a single OutlinedTextField labelled '6-digit code' rather than a segmented 6-box OTP field, which is the category convention for Indian consumer apps.
Off-grid icon sizing within a single button group: the Google mark is 22dp while the sibling Email and Phone icons are 20dp.
EmailEntry stacks three full-width TextButtons (mode toggle, forgot password, plus the back button above the form), producing an undifferentiated ladder of low-contrast text links.

error.quality: MAJOR ABSENCE AND A SILENT-FAILURE BUG. ConsentUiState carries an `error: String?` field (customer-app/app/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/customer/ui/consent/ConsentUiState.kt:8) and the ViewModel populates it on both onConfirm and onDeclineAll failure (ConsentViewModel.kt:82, :103), but a full read of all 556 lines of DpdpConsentScreen.kt shows the screen never reads uiState.error. A failed consent write therefore just stops the spinner and leaves the user on the same screen with no feedback — on a legally mandated gate.

offline.quality: No offline branch; a network-backed consent write failure lands in the unrendered error field.

i18n.hindiRisk: HIGH. (a) Font sizes are pinned in sp and override the type scale: 26sp hero title (:284), 14sp hero subtitle (:292), 14sp toggle title (:495), 12sp toggle description (:501), 12sp legal copy (:525, :536, :545), 16sp CTA (:431). Devanagari has taller ascenders/descenders and 12sp legal copy in Hindi is at the edge of legibility. (b) The primary CTA is a fixed 56dp-tall Button (:411) containing a single Text with no maxLines — the Hindi label 'सहमत हों और जारी रखें' (values-hi/strings.xml:239) is materially longer than 'Agree and continue' and will wrap-then-clip inside the fixed height. INFERRED. (c) Each ConsentToggleRow is a fixed Row with the text column at weight(1f) between a 44dp tile and a Switch (:474, :489, :507), so longer Hindi descriptions such as values-hi/strings.xml:231 force extra wrapping and desynchronise the three row heights. (d) The 112dp bottom reservation (:211) is computed for English content height.
i18n.currencyFormatting: N/A — no money is rendered on this screen (verified across all 556 lines).

contentDescriptions.note: Both Icons in the file are contentDescription = null — the hero brand icon (:272) and every ConsentToggleRow category icon (:481).

touchTargetRisks.note: The toggle Row itself has no toggleable/clickable modifier (:464-470) — only the trailing Switch (:507) accepts input, so the title and description text are dead to touch. On a 44dp icon + text + switch row this is a large visually-interactive-looking area that does nothing.
'Reject all' is a bare TextButton with no minimum height set; it is the legally required decline path and is the least prominent control on the screen.

contrastRisks.note: CRITICAL DARK-MODE FAILURE: ConsentToggleRow hardcodes the title colour to TEXT_PRIMARY_LIGHT (#18231F) even though the parent computed a dark-aware textPrimary at :196 and never passes it in. In dark mode the card background is #1A2E24 (:73) so near-black title text sits on a near-black card.
Same defect for the toggle description, hardcoded to TextMuted (#5F6C66) against the #1A2E24 dark card.

'Reject all' is hardcoded to TextMuted (#5F6C66) in both themes — on the #1A2E24 dark CTA background it is barely legible, and even in light mode it is low-contrast small text for a mandatory legal choice.
Hero subtitle at Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.70f) over a gradient.
Legal copy at 12sp in textMuted, centered — smallest text on the screen and it carries the DPDP consent language.

a11y.focusOrder: No HsScreenTitle and no semantics { heading() } anywhere in the file — neither the hero title (:279) nor the 'Data use consent' section heading (:321) is exposed as a heading. Because the Row is not toggleable (:464), TalkBack announces the title, the description, and the Switch as three separate unlinked nodes, so the switch has no accessible label tying it to its category. INFERRED.

placeholderOrMissing: No painterResource / Image / R.drawable in the file. The hero's only figurative element is Icons.Default.Eco — a generic Material leaf glyph — standing in for brand identity on the app's first screen, and it does not appear on any other onboarding surface.

animationsUsed.what: Material3 Switch default thumb slide (the only motion on the screen, inherited from the component)

motion.transitionsOnNav: None. No animate*/AnimatedVisibility/Crossfade in the file; the loading spinner appears by a hard `if` swap inside the button (:419). Navigation away is a default NavHost transition (AppNavigation.kt:185-188).

surfaces.density: Dense and unevenly rhythmed. Card padding is 28/20/20 (:313-317) while the CTA bar uses 20/16 (:401) and the hero uses 24 (:256) — three different gutters on one screen. Toggle rows are 10dp vertical (:468) separated by dividers with only 4dp of padding (:347), which reads cramped next to the 16dp Spacers at :333 and :380. The hero, at a nominal 40% of screen height with only an icon and two lines of text, is by contrast very airy.

observations.claim: ConsentToggleRow hardcodes its title and description colours to the light-theme values while the parent composable computes dark-aware colours and never passes them down, so in dark mode near-black text (#18231F) renders on a near-black card (#1A2E24) — the three consent options become unreadable.
The screen never renders ConsentUiState.error, which the ViewModel does populate on failure — a failed consent write on a legally mandated gate produces zero user feedback.

The file completely bypasses the design system: ~20 private Color literals (:68-89, :143-144) and ~40 raw Int dp/sp constants (:95-145) redefine the palette and spacing scale locally, and three of the redefined colours (#0D1A16, #1A2E24, #EDE8E3) do not match the real tokens they duplicate.
Dark mode is detected by inspecting the red channel of the background colour (background.red < 0.5) rather than by reading the theme — a heuristic that silently breaks if the palette ever changes.

The hero uses fillMaxHeight(0.40f) inside a verticalScroll Column; a scrollable parent passes an unbounded height constraint, so fillMaxHeight has no bounded height to take a fraction of and the hero collapses to its content height instead of the intended 40% — the designed hero proportion is not what renders.

Three consecutive first-run screens each render a different hero: consent is a centered-icon 40% hero with three glows and hardcoded colours, the language picker is a bottom-aligned 30% hero with two glows, and auth is a bottom-aligned 38% hero with two glows — and only consent omits the 'HomeHeroo' wordmark entirely.

The sticky CTA bar is not given navigationBarsPadding, and the scroll body reserves only 112dp for a bar that measures roughly 136dp (16 + 56 + 8 + TextButton + 16), so the legal copy can be occluded by the CTA bar and the CTA bar by the gesture bar.

The mandatory 'Reject all' path is a low-contrast grey TextButton hardcoded to #5F6C66 in both themes, visually subordinated beneath a 56dp ExtraBold brand-green Agree button — a dark-pattern-adjacent hierarchy on a DPDP consent gate.
Consent rows are not tappable — only the Switch itself accepts input; the icon tile, title, and description are inert.

The legal copy is rendered with BasicText and a bare TextStyle(textAlign) rather than a MaterialTheme typography slot, so it inherits the platform default font family (Roboto) instead of Geist/Noto, at 12sp.
The primary CTA label uses the unmapped titleMedium slot, so the single most important button in the consent gate renders in Roboto while the rest of the app renders in Geist.
The privacy policy link points at https://homeservices.app/privacy, a hardcoded URL using the placeholder project name, while the product brands itself 'HomeHeroo' two screens later.
The category icon tiles introduce a blue (#1A4B8C) and an orange (#E65100) that exist nowhere in the design system, and their pale backgrounds are light-only so they do not adapt in dark mode.
The Switch is coloured with stock Material 2 values (#C8E6C9 checked track, #E0E0E0 unchecked track) rather than the brand palette.
Icons.Default.Eco (a leaf) is used as the hero symbol for a data-privacy consent screen — semantically wrong iconography on the app's first impression.

composition: Scaffold with a Material3 TopAppBar (WaitlistScreen.kt:41-54)
TopAppBar title = HsScreenTitle(stringResource(waitlist_title)) — i.e. the sentence 'Get notified when we expand' as an app-bar title (:44)
Navigation icon: AutoMirrored ArrowBack IconButton with contentDescription taken from R.string.service_detail_back_desc (:46-51)

Body = WaitlistScreenContent, padded by the Scaffold insets (:56-65). All remaining structure lives in customer-app/app/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/customer/ui/waitlist/WaitlistScreenContent.kt (206 lines):
Root Column, 24dp horizontal padding, navigationBarsPadding (WaitlistScreenContent.kt:45-51)
24dp Spacer (:52)
WaitlistHeader — headlineMedium Bold title (the SAME waitlist_title string already in the app bar), 8dp Spacer, bodyLarge/onSurfaceVariant body copy (:53, component :183-196)
32dp Spacer (:54)
Then a `when (uiState)` over five states (:56-104):

Form — OutlinedTextField phone with a hardcoded '+91 98765 43210' placeholder, 24dp Spacer, full-width HsPrimaryButton 'Join the waitlist' gated on isPhoneValid (:92-103; PhoneField :108-123, SubmitButton :125-136)
Submitting — the same phone field but disabled, 24dp Spacer, a bare centered CircularProgressIndicator (:63-64, component :171-181)
Confirmed — a primaryContainer Surface with MaterialTheme.shapes.medium, 24dp padding, a 48dp CheckCircle icon, titleLarge SemiBold headline, and bodyMedium body (:57, component :138-169)

Error — phone field, 8dp Spacer, the raw reason string in bodyMedium/error colour, 24dp Spacer, HsPrimaryButton whose label flips between 'Try again' and 'Join the waitlist' and which is DISABLED when !retryable (:66-90)

loading.quality: BARE CENTERED SPINNER. The submit button is removed entirely and replaced by a default CircularProgressIndicator in a Box, so the CTA disappears rather than entering a loading state.

error.quality: POOR. The body is uiState.reason, which the ViewModel fills with throwable.message — a raw exception string surfaced verbatim to the user (customer-app/app/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/customer/ui/waitlist/WaitlistViewModel.kt:103). It is rendered as plain red body text with no icon, container, or structure.

success.quality: The best-realised state on the screen — a primaryContainer card with a 48dp check icon and a headline/body pair. But it is a terminal dead end: no CTA back to browsing, and the app-bar back arrow is the only exit.

offline.quality: MAJOR ABSENCE. No offline branch in WaitlistUiState (customer-app/app/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/customer/ui/waitlist/WaitlistUiState.kt:3-21); network failure becomes a retryable Error carrying the exception text.

skeletonOrSpinner.note: Bare default spinner, centered, no size/colour override, replacing the submit button. No HsSkeletonBlock usage.

hardcodedDp.context: Confirmed check-icon size (equals space12 but written as a literal)

hardcodedUserFacingStrings.text: Session expired. Please sign in again.
Please enter a valid Indian mobile number (+91XXXXXXXXXX).

i18n.hindiRisk: MEDIUM-HIGH. (a) The three error reasons above are Kotlin literals in WaitlistViewModel.kt (:41, :76, :103) and are rendered directly at WaitlistScreenContent.kt:74, so Hindi users see English error copy. (b) waitlist_title is a full sentence ('विस्तार होने पर सूचना पाएँ', values-hi/strings.xml:472) used as a TopAppBar title (WaitlistScreen.kt:44) — Material3 single-line app-bar titles clip, and HsScreenTitle is called without maxLines/overflow so it defaults to TextOverflow.Clip (HsScreenTitle.kt:34). INFERRED. (c) The root Column has no verticalScroll (WaitlistScreenContent.kt:45-51), so longer Hindi header copy plus the field, error line, and button cannot scroll and will be clipped on small screens with the IME open — there is also no imePadding.
i18n.currencyFormatting: N/A — no money is rendered (verified across both files, 67 + 206 lines).

contentDescriptions.note: The back arrow is described, but it borrows R.string.service_detail_back_desc from an unrelated screen. The Confirmed check icon is contentDescription = null (WaitlistScreenContent.kt:151), so the success signal is invisible to TalkBack apart from the text.

contrastRisks.note: Error text uses colorScheme.error (#D73C3C) on background #FBF7EF at bodyMedium — red-on-cream small text (WaitlistScreenContent.kt:76).
RateLimited text uses the same error red at bodyLarge (WaitlistScreenContent.kt:204).

a11y.focusOrder: HsScreenTitle marks the TopAppBar title as a heading (WaitlistScreen.kt:44), but the duplicate on-screen H1 at WaitlistScreenContent.kt:185 is a plain Text with no heading semantics, so TalkBack sees one heading and then an unlabelled repeat of the same sentence.

placeholderOrMissing: No painterResource / Image / R.drawable in either file. The only graphic on the entire screen is the 48dp Material CheckCircle glyph in the success state — the Form state, which is what most users see, is a completely image-free wall of text plus one input.

motion.transitionsOnNav: None. No animate*/AnimatedVisibility/Crossfade in either file. Form -> Submitting -> Confirmed hard-cuts between three different layouts, so the success moment — the emotional payoff of the whole screen — arrives with no motion at all.

surfaces.density: Airy at the top, empty at the bottom. 24dp side padding with 24/32dp stacked spacers (WaitlistScreenContent.kt:49, :52, :54) pushes the single input roughly a third of the way down, and because the Column has no weight/Spacer arrangement everything is top-aligned, leaving the entire lower half of the screen blank in every state. The RateLimited state is a single line of red text on an otherwise empty screen.

observations.claim: Raw exception text is surfaced to the user as error copy: the ViewModel puts throwable.message into uiState.reason and the screen renders it verbatim.
The RateLimited state is a dead end — it renders one line of red text and removes the phone field, the submit button, and every other affordance, leaving the user with no action but the back arrow.

The session-expired path sets a non-retryable Error, which renders an enabled-looking phone field above a DISABLED 'Join the waitlist' button and an English-only 'Session expired' message, with no sign-in CTA — an unrecoverable screen.

This screen has no hero, no gradient, no card shell and no design-system framing at all, so it looks like it belongs to a different product than the consent/language/auth screens it sits alongside — plain text on a flat background with one outlined field.
The same string (waitlist_title, a full sentence) is rendered twice on one screen — once as the TopAppBar title and again as the in-body headline directly beneath it.
The submit CTA vanishes during submission and is replaced by a bare centered spinner rather than the button entering a loading state.
The phone placeholder '+91 98765 43210' is a hardcoded literal rather than a string resource, and it is duplicated verbatim in strings.xml as auth_mobile_placeholder for the auth screen.

The form Column has neither verticalScroll nor imePadding, so with the numeric keyboard open on a small device the header, error line, and submit button can be pushed off-screen with no way to scroll to them.
The Confirmed state is terminal with no forward CTA — after joining the waitlist the only exit is the back arrow.
Phone validation is silent until submit: the field shows no isError styling or supporting text, only the submit button's enabled flag reflects validity.
The back-button contentDescription is borrowed from an unrelated screen's string (service_detail_back_desc).
Zero motion — the success card appears by a hard state swap with no entrance animation.
